sq.QUESTION_DESC: An elastic string is stretched between two points at a distance \(\pi \) apart. In its equilibrium position the string is in the shape of the curve \(f(x)=k(sin x - sin^3 x)\). Obtain \(y(x,t)\) the vertical displacement if \(y\) satisfies the equation \({\partial^2y \over \partial t^2}={\partial^2 y \over \partial x^2}\)

A tightly stretched string with fixed end points \(x=0\) and \(x=l\) is initially in a position given by \(y(x,0)=y_0 sin^3 {\pi x \over l}\). If it is released from rest from this position find the displacement \(y\) at any distance \(x\) from one end at any time \(t\).

Hint: The boundary conditions are: \((i) y(0,t)=0, \forall t>0 \\ (ii) y(l,t)=0, \forall t>0 \\ (iii) {\partial y(x,0) \over \partial t }=0, \forall x \\ (iv) y(x,0)=y_0 sin ^3 {\pi x \over l}.\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{Wave equation with BCs: \(y(0,t)=0\), \(y(l,t)=0\), \(y_t(x,0)=0\), \(y(x,0)= a \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{General solution: \(y(x,t)= \sum \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right)\left[C_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)+D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(y_t(x,0)=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_n=0.\) So \(y(x,t)= \sum C_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(y(x,0)= \sum C_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) = a \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{By orthogonality, \(C_1 = a\), and \(C_n=0\) for \(n\neq1\).}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Thus \(y(x,t)= a \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{This is a standing wave: spatial part \(\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right)\) fixed, temporal part \(\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi c t}{l}\right)\) oscillates.}\) (3 Marks)
\(\text{Nodes at \(x=0, l\) (always zero). Antinode at \(x=l/2\) with amplitude \(a|\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi c t}{l}\right)|.\)}\) (2 Marks)
Explain standing vs traveling wave: no propagation of shape, only oscillation in time. (1 Mark)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A string of length  \(l\)  is fixed at both ends. It is displaced initially as \( y(x,0)= a \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right)\)}\\ \text{and released from rest. Find the displacement  $y(x,t). $ Show that the solution represents a standing wave.}\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{Case 1: \(y(x,0)=0\), \(y_t(x,0)= v_0 \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{General solution: \(y(x,t)= \sum \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right)\left[C_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)+D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(y(x,0)=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(C_n=0.\) So \(y(x,t)= \sum D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{\(y_t(x,0)= \sum D_n \left(\dfrac{n\pi c}{l}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) = v_0 \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{Thus \(D_2 \left(\dfrac{2\pi c}{l}\right) = v_0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_2 = \dfrac{v_0 l}{2\pi c}.\) Other \(D_n=0.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{So \(y(x,t)= \dfrac{v_0 l}{2\pi c} \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{l}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{Case 2: \(y_t(x,0)= v_0 \sin^3\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right) = \dfrac{v_0}{4}\left[3 \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right) - \sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi x}{l}\right)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Similarly, \(y(x,t)= \sum D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{Then \(y_t(x,0)= \sum D_n \left(\dfrac{n\pi c}{l}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) = \dfrac{v_0}{4}\left[3 \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right) - \sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi x}{l}\right)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Equate: For \(n=1\): \(D_1 \left(\dfrac{\pi c}{l}\right)= \dfrac{3v_0}{4}\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_1 = \dfrac{3v_0 l}{4\pi c}.\) For \(n=3\): \(D_3 \left(\dfrac{3\pi c}{l}\right) = -\dfrac{v_0}{4}\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_3 = -\dfrac{v_0 l}{12\pi c}.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Thus \(y(x,t)= \dfrac{3v_0 l}{4\pi c} \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi c t}{l}\right) - \dfrac{v_0 l}{12\pi c} \sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi x}{l}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark)
